question: Looking back at your completed task, how did you decide what to read or request next, and when you had enough information to answer? Give a brief account of observable choices and the information you expected further reads to provide.
response: I read the common guide, then requested package query --help to learn the search syntax and candidate limit. The help did not define the dependency filters, so I requested package query --explain and read its embedded depends, dependency-target, and dependency-depth facets. Those showed that an exact depends term without depth tests direct dependencies and that dependency-target=net10.0 selects the applicable manifest group. I then ran one Microsoft.Extensions.* search with --take 40 and those filters. The result contained a matching package, its selected framework group, and a direct Polly manifest row. I read stderr to understand whether the search exhausted the family; it said CandidateLimitReached. That supplied the package evidence and the necessary coverage caveat. Another package detail read could have repeated the manifest evidence, while more searching would have gone beyond the 40-candidate bound, so I stopped.
